input.raw_text: The Fed's hawkish turn is doing real damage now, and the selling is no longer contained to the speculative corners. The unprofitable tech trade has bled for months, but this week the knife turned on the megacaps — the likes of Nvidia and Tesla are breaking technical levels and the dip-buyers who rescued every pullback last year are simply absent. I watch the two-year make higher highs every morning as the market prices a more aggressive hiking path, and every tick takes another leg out of duration-heavy growth. What strikes me most is the absence of panic: no capitulation volume, no VIX above 30, just a relentless grind that bleeds out anyone who bought the last dip. Managers are cutting winners to raise cash because their losers are unsellable. The buy-every-correction playbook is dead, and I suspect more air comes out before this finds a floor.
input.summary: A more restrictive Federal Reserve outlook and rising two-year yields are broadening equity weakness from unprofitable technology companies into megacap growth companies. Subdued volatility and limited capitulation characterize a persistent, orderly decline, while absent support during pullbacks and cash raising through sales of liquid winners suggest strained market liquidity. The timing and extent of stabilization remain uncertain.

observations.statement: Equity weakness spreading beyond speculative technology companies
Megacap growth companies breaking notable technical levels
Two-year Treasury yields reaching successive highs
Higher yields pressuring duration-sensitive growth companies
Limited support appearing during equity pullbacks
Persistent decline without capitulation volume or extreme volatility
Liquid winners being sold to raise cash amid illiquid losers
